project.name: TanSail Homepage Proof Modules
project.audience: Builders evaluating TanSail and maintainers adapting its reusable landing blocks
project.outcome: Make the verified technology foundation, supported site scenarios, and replaceable testimonial composition immediately understandable

hierarchy: A short centered label introduces a broad, low-height ecosystem band
Technology names carry more visual weight than surrounding explanatory copy
typography: Compact neutral labels support larger recognizable technology names
color: A quiet near-white canvas lets small colored marks punctuate mostly dark wordmarks
interaction: The ecosystem reads at a glance and can collapse into a horizontally scrollable rail
avoid: Do not reuse third-party logos, their exact ordering, or the source spacing and two-row composition

hierarchy: A large editorial heading introduces a dense wall of human-sized quote cards
Variable quote lengths create an informal masonry rhythm
typography: Large serif display type contrasts with practical sans-serif quotes and identity labels
color: Warm white cards and hairline borders keep a long social-proof section calm
interaction: The section is primarily readable content and does not depend on hover interactions
avoid: Do not copy quotes, personal names, avatars, roles, card geometry, or imply that sample content is verified evidence

hierarchy: A clear outcome-led heading is followed by category controls and a compact card directory
Filters establish the information model before detailed cards
typography: Large language-aware display copy leads into short labels and bilingual technical terms
color: A restrained accent color links filters and card metadata without coloring every surface
interaction: Category chips filter the visible catalog while preserving a simple reading order
avoid: Do not reuse the scientific product copy, tool marks, pink palette, clipped carousel, or exact card arrangement

direction.name: Evidence Harbor
principles: Separate verified technology facts from illustrative template content
Let visitors scan compatibility and scenarios before reading detailed proof
Keep every module reusable through typed configuration and bilingual content
materials: Opaque editorial cards on the existing Luminous Harbor canvas
Original lettermarks, semantic accent tones, hairline borders, and restrained shadows
Compact filter pills reserved for interaction rather than decoration
proof: Technology names verified from the TanSail dependency and deployment configuration
Scenario descriptions bounded by the six maintained recipes and browser-only core
Testimonials visibly marked as replaceable sample content until verified feedback exists

transformations: Replace every third-party logo with an original typographic lettermark and verified technology label
Use a responsive semantic grid and rail instead of reproducing either reference logo layout
Turn the tool directory into TanSail site-scenario filters with original categories and copy
Use an accessible three-column card flow with explicit sample badges instead of presenting fabricated social proof
Place the modules inside TanSail's hero-to-delivery narrative rather than following the reference section order
